scenarios.description: The management host receives a lease on a different subnet while the Catalyst remains at its documented address.
scenarios.purpose: Prove that a host-side network transition is classified without blaming the switch or VLAN.

phases.transition: The original directly connected management path is healthy.
DHCP moves the same adapter off the historical management prefix.

scenarios.description: DHCP renews the selected adapter without changing its address or management prefix.
scenarios.purpose: Ensure an ordinary renewal is not misclassified as a management-path failure.

phases.transition: The direct path is healthy before renewal.
The lease timestamp changes but the selected path stays healthy.

scenarios.description: Windows can no longer select an IPv4 source address or route for the Catalyst target.
scenarios.purpose: Classify missing host-route evidence distinctly from a device outage.

phases.transition: The management route is present.
The selected IPv4 route disappears.

scenarios.description: A scoped route through a documentation gateway takes precedence for the Catalyst target.
scenarios.purpose: Preserve uncertainty when a valid explicit route exists but the destination is unreachable.

phases.transition: The management target is directly connected.
A scoped route becomes preferred and the SSH probe times out.

scenarios.description: Windows changes from the proven Ethernet adapter to Wi-Fi and sends the target through a default gateway.
scenarios.purpose: Detect a host adapter transition while preserving the lower confidence caused by identity discontinuity.

phases.transition: Ethernet owns the healthy management path.
Wi-Fi becomes the selected adapter after the management session fails.

scenarios.description: TCP port 22 remains reachable while the serialized SSH session is stale.
scenarios.purpose: Avoid treating a half-open session symptom as proof of a device or VLAN failure.

phases.transition: TCP and the serialized session are healthy.
The session becomes stale although TCP still accepts connections.

scenarios.description: The network path reaches SSH but Catalyst credentials are rejected.
scenarios.purpose: Keep typed authentication failure separate from reachability and recovery planning.

phases.transition: Authentication initially succeeds.
The session reports its typed authentication error.

scenarios.description: The Catalyst presents a different SSH host key after a healthy session.
scenarios.purpose: Prove that trust failure blocks automated recovery and remains explicitly classified.

phases.transition: The pinned host key is trusted.
The session refuses the changed key.

scenarios.description: The same confirmed local endpoint moves from one access port to another.
scenarios.purpose: Retain stable endpoint identity, update the current attachment, and preserve the prior attachment as history.

phases.transition: The confirmed endpoint is attached to Gi0/2.
The same hardware identity is re-observed on Gi0/5.

scenarios.description: A different confirmed hardware identity appears on the previously occupied access port.
scenarios.purpose: Distinguish replacement from movement and retain the former identity only as historical evidence.

phases.transition: The original endpoint occupies Gi0/2.
A different confirmed identity occupies Gi0/2.

scenarios.description: The same learned address is simultaneously visible through two access ports.
scenarios.purpose: Represent ambiguous attachment evidence without duplicating a stable endpoint or fabricating movement.

phases.transition: One learned address is initially unique to Gi0/2.
The learned address appears through both ports in one observation.

scenarios.description: Current Meraki Dashboard evidence becomes unavailable while the direct Catalyst path remains healthy.
scenarios.purpose: Treat provider loss as missing corroboration rather than proof of device failure.

phases.transition: Current Meraki LAN evidence accompanies a healthy path.
Dashboard requests fail but direct host and SSH evidence remains healthy.

scenarios.description: Current Meraki LAN configuration makes a historical direct-path interpretation unsafe.
scenarios.purpose: Require indeterminate classification when current configured routing context conflicts with a host-only recovery inference.

phases.transition: The host and Catalyst share the original management LAN.
Current Meraki evidence reports both host and target LANs while SSH remains unreachable.

scenarios.description: The management service is reconstructed between a healthy observation and a subnet transition.
scenarios.purpose: Prove that durable last-known-good evidence survives process/service reconstruction with its original timestamp.

phases.transition: A healthy observation is committed to the temporary history store.
A reconstructed service observes the same adapter on another subnet.

scenarios.description: A blocked recovery plan is retained while DHCP changes the bound primary address and observation timestamp.
scenarios.purpose: Demonstrate that a previously generated plan fails state-binding validation before any execution authority exists.

phases.transition: The original path establishes last-known-good evidence.
A subnet change produces a bounded, non-executable recovery plan.
DHCP changes the bound address before the prior plan can be used.

scenarios.description: The host observer explicitly reports internally conflicting route/source evidence.
scenarios.purpose: Fail closed when normalized evidence is incomplete or contradictory instead of choosing a confident root cause.

phases.transition: The evidence sources initially agree.
Normalization rejects the conflicting source and route evidence.

scenarios.description: A removed management route is restored and SwitchOps returns to a healthy understanding.
scenarios.purpose: Prove the product recovers its own model after the environment becomes healthy again, and that the plan built while degraded no longer binds.

phases.transition: The management path is healthy.
The selected IPv4 route disappears.
The route returns and the path is healthy again.

scenarios.description: A confirmed endpoint briefly disconnects and returns to the same access port.
scenarios.purpose: Prove a brief absence does not create a second endpoint or a false movement claim.

phases.transition: The confirmed endpoint is attached to Gi0/2.
The endpoint disconnects and no MAC is learned.
The same hardware identity returns to Gi0/2.

scenarios.description: A confirmed endpoint disconnects and reappears on a different access port.
scenarios.purpose: Prove a cable move across an absence is reconciled as movement of one identity, not a replacement.

phases.transition: The confirmed endpoint is attached to Gi0/2.
The cable is unplugged and the endpoint is not observed.
The same hardware identity appears on Gi0/5.

scenarios.description: DHCP stops answering, Windows self-assigns a link-local address, and the lease is later restored.
scenarios.purpose: Prove an APIPA fallback is classified as a host-side path fault and that recovery returns the model to healthy.

phases.transition: A normal DHCP lease is held.
No DHCP server answers and Windows self-assigns 169.254.0.0/16.
DHCP answers again and the original prefix is restored.

scenarios.description: The Catalyst stops answering while the host path stays intact, then returns.
scenarios.purpose: Prove SwitchOps reports an indeterminate device-or-path outcome rather than asserting a device state it cannot observe, and reconnects to the same identity.

phases.transition: The device is reachable and the session is live.
The device stops answering while the host route stays on-link.
The device answers again on the same attachment.

scenarios.description: A blocked recovery plan is retained while the selected route changes underneath it.
scenarios.purpose: Prove plan state-binding rejects a route change, not only an address change.

phases.transition: The original path establishes last-known-good evidence.
The host leaves the management prefix and a bounded plan is produced.
A different gateway takes over the default route before the plan could be used.

scenarios.description: Anonymized replay of the observed incident in which the host acquired a lease on a different prefix while the Catalyst stayed on its historical management prefix.
scenarios.purpose: Regression-lock the real diagnosis: same Catalyst identity, no unsupported device-offline claim, recovery planned but blocked.

phases.transition: The recorded last-known-good management path.
The observed incident state.

scenarios.description: The host regains an on-link address in the Catalyst management prefix and management recovers.
scenarios.purpose: Prove SwitchOps reconciles back to healthy once the management path exists again, and that a plan produced while degraded no longer binds. The restoration is modelled as an environment change: SwitchOps has no executor and performs no part of it.

phases.transition: The host is on the Catalyst management prefix and management is healthy.
The host acquires a lease on a different prefix and the target follows the default route.
An on-link path to the management prefix exists again and TCP/22 answers.
